speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: asked the Minister for Transport for upcoming rail lines, whether there are any plans to open the rail market to new operators beyond the two existing operators.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: However, we also need to consider the unique circumstances and characteristics of the rail industry.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The rail industry is a highly complex and large-scale system that delivers an essential service.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: So, we must allow for operators to reap economies of scale even as they maintain high reliability and service standards.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
text: So, any decision pertaining to current and new rail lines, will have to continue to balance these key considerations.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I have just got two quick supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The first is in relation to my original Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Am I right to understand that, at this moment, there are no plans to actually bring in potential foreign players to enter the market, just like what the Government did when it comes to the bus business?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The second clarification is, I do hear the Minister's point on the large-scale system, that is, the MRT networks and all.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, given the requirements for economies of scale and efficiencies at the same time, if we are not bringing in the foreign players, would the Government also consider perhaps having just a single operator to manage the entire rail line to achieve those economies of scale?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In his two questions, I think he has actually traversed the entire spectrum of what could be the industry structure – from a monopoly to competitions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I am not quite sure where he is on the spectrum.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, specific to the Members' second question, these are all policy design.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As for the involvement of foreign players, I think the way the Member has framed it perhaps may not be an entirely correct characterisation.
